one-check-per-line.why: all 4 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 4

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: all 4 lines quoted in the builder brief

words-only.why: Each of the four verifier checks only tests what its expect line requires. Check 1 passes if the greeting for the name prints "in upper case". Comparing it to the upper-cased normal output is just what "the greeting" means. Check 2 compares the head output with the base output exactly, which is what "unchanged" requires. Check 3 asks that docs/index.md mention --shout and explain it, which is a fair reading of "documents". Check 4 requires "the PR is merged and the fetched published page lists --shout", which is what "after merge... lists --shout" requires. Its FAIL rule for an unmerged PR only reports the line as not yet shown and adds nothing stricter. The stricter items are all under "Advisory (not pass/fail conditions)": npm test, the flag placed after the name, exact outputs, the exit code and pages.yml. None of them appears in a PASS or FAIL condition.

runs-as-written.why: Most commands are fine. `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada`, `'Grace Hopper'` and `Ada --shout` use bin/greet.js, which exists. `npm test` maps to the "node --test" script. `cat docs/index.md` and `grep -n -- '--shout' docs/index.md` are valid. `gh run list --workflow pages.yml` names a workflow that exists, and `curl -sSL https://o.github.io/greet-cli/` is valid. The criterion breaks on the verifier's Check 4 command `gh pr view <number> --json state,mergedAt`. It would not run as written: the shell reads `<number>` as input redirection from a file named "number", which doesn't exist, so the command fails before gh starts. The verifier has to replace it with a real PR number (or drop it), so not every command the briefs give runs as written.

catches-traps.why:
Item 2 is handled. Check 2 runs `node bin/greet.js Ada` at the PR head and "the same commands at the PR's base commit" and then compares the outputs, so it does not rely only on a hand-written string.

Item 1 is not handled. Check 4 reads the live page: "fetch the page (`curl -sSL https://o.github.io/greet-cli/`) and search it for `--shout`". If the PR isn't merged, it says to report "FAIL". It never says that at the PR head the check should confirm that docs/index.md lists --shout and that pages.yml publishes docs/ from main. pages.yml comes up only in an advisory note ("If the PR changes that, line 4 is at risk"), which isn't a pass/fail check. So the check for line 4 still points at the live page instead of checking at the head what will publish it.

avoids-must-not.why: I checked verifier Check 4 against both must_not items. It does not silently PASS: it asks for evidence and reports FAIL when the PR is not merged, so item 2 is avoided. Item 1 is broken. Check 4 says to "fetch the page (`curl -sSL https://o.github.io/greet-cli/`) and search it for `--shout`", then gives "PASS: the PR is merged and the fetched published page lists --shout" and "FAIL: the fetched page does not list --shout." That is a pass/fail on what the live page shows today. The merge-status gate doesn't fix this: the result still depends on the live site, not on the PR head the verifier is meant to check. Line 4 should have been treated as a post-merge item that can't be checked yet. Instead it is judged by fetching the live page. The builder brief is fine here, since it only notes that line 4 is confirmed after merge.

methods-private.why: I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief, looking for probes that appear in both. The builder brief contains several. Its step 2 says "`node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` prints `HELLO, ADA!`". That is the same input and expected output as verifier Check 1, which runs `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` and expects `HELLO, ADA!`. Its step 3 says "`node bin/greet.js Ada` still prints `Hello, Ada!\n`", which matches the verifier's advisory expected exact outputs. Step 4 tells the builder to add tests for `--shout Ada` and `Ada --shout`, which repeats the verifier's probe inputs, including the advisory `node bin/greet.js Ada --shout`. Step 2 also says to keep the usage message and exit code, which mirrors the verifier's advisory check for exit 2 with `usage: greet <name>`. Running the expect line's own command or writing tests is allowed. Giving the builder the verifier's exact inputs and expected outputs is not, so the builder brief carries the checker's probes.
